source.note: CoreDNS publishes NO Kubernetes compatibility matrix in its repo (README.md and plugin/kubernetes/README.md checked at the pinned tag) — supportWindows is deliberately OMITTED, so every cluster running CoreDNS gets the honest NO_VENDOR_DATA INFO finding and a PARTIAL addon-compat tier. The kubeadm-pinned CoreDNS-version-per-k8s-release table (kubernetes/kubernetes constants, coredns/deployment CoreDNS-k8s_version.md) is a statement of what kubeadm SHIPS, not a support window, and was deliberately not transcribed as one. With no matrix the hop is the opt-in CURRENCY hop (currencyHop=true) to latestKnownVersion — the newest release note at the pinned tag — and every surface says it is NOT required by the Kubernetes upgrade. Caveat stated rather than hidden: on kubeadm, k3s and RKE2 the Kubernetes upgrade itself bumps the bundled CoreDNS, so the CURRENCY framing is exact only for separately-managed installs (EKS add-on, Helm chart); the rules selected for the hop are the same either way. Since 2026-09-10 this entry carries ZERO hand-written rules/upgradeNotes: the release notes are extracted mechanically into scripts/readiness-agent/kb/coredns/notes-<minor>.md (extract-coredns-notes.py, tag v1.14.7, floor 1.5) and the rules live in src/main/resources/k8s-rules/coredns/ (sourceId coredns, hop-scoped). The federation/proxy removal rules that used to live here as crSpecListContains now read the same agent projection (corednsPlugins on kube-system *coredns* ConfigMaps — directive NAMES only, Corefile values are never collected) through SPEC_PATH_MATCHES; rows synced by an agent predating that projection read NOT_DETECTABLE, never CLEARED. Detection: the three suffixes cover registry.k8s.io/coredns/coredns, Docker Hub coredns/coredns, EKS's eks/coredns and Rancher's mirrored-coredns-coredns (k3s/RKE2 — the box cluster); the pre-k8s-1.21 single-segment k8s.gcr.io/coredns repo is still a known miss, because a bare 'coredns' suffix would also match any repo merely ending in those letters.
